To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the lactose utilization gene cluster of S. thermophilis is organized as an operons, (ii) the amino acid sequences of the beta-galcotisidase from S. thermophileus and L. bulgarius are very homologous, (iii) the amino acid sequence of S. thermophile is homologous to those from E.coli and Klebsiela pneumoniae
the beta-gal genes are organized in the same order in both S. thermophilous and L. bulgarius, and that the proteins share conserved regions.
the lacZ sequences of two strains of Streptococcus were compared and found to differ at 21 nucleotide positions, of which only 9 resulted in amino acid differences in the proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning of lacZ from two strains of S. thermophilis and the determination of their nucleotide sequence and the amino acid sequence of their beta-galactoisidase.
the cloning of the lacZ gene from the S. thermophillus ATCC 19285 strain and with the analysis of this gene.
the molecular biology of lactose utilization by S. thermophilis, a micro-organism widely used as a starter for yogurt production.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lacZ genes from S. thermophiles A054 and ATCC 19285 have been isolated and characterized.
the S. thermophiles beta-galacto-sidase is a protein with 35% identity to the E. coli protein and 48% identity to the L. bulgaricu s beta-galactosi-dases.
the lacZ gene from the S. thermophillus A054 strain was cloned and its DNA sequence was determined, showing a 99.3% identity with the lacZ gene of the S. Thermophilus ATCC strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lacZ gene from the S. thermophillus A054 strain is highly similar to the lacZ gene of S. thermophilous ATCC 19285.
the lacZ gene is a useful genetic marker for the study of the S.thermophilus species.
the S. thermophillus beta-galactase is more similar to the beta-gal from E. coli than to the beta-gals from L. bulgaricas and K. pneumoniae, which are more similar to each other.
